continuity.teaching_arc: Manu's peaceful devotion leads into Kardama's long austerity, Narayana's promise, Kardama and Devahuti's household life, Kapila's birth and teaching, and the poet's healing prayer.
continuity.recurring_figures: Keep Kardama, Devahuti, Manu, Shatarupa and Kapila visually consistent across their appearances. Treat the nine daughters as nine distinct young women only where the verse requires them. Narayana is the deep-blue four-armed Lord with consistent attributes. Kapila is the same divine identity expressed as a human-like sage child/teacher, not a second simultaneous Vishnu figure. Bhattathiri is the older clean-shaven devotee defined in his character bible.
continuity.style: Use the series bible's matte Kerala temple-mural style: firm contour, shallow space, broad earthy ochre, cream, maroon and olive fields, restrained painted ochre ornament. Reference images guide scene meaning only; recompose each as an original 16:9 mural. No readable text, glossy skin, metallic effects, cinematic lighting, outer border or duplication.
continuity.orientation_policy: Landscape 16:9 candidates only. Portrait compositions remain paused.
continuity.reference_policy: Use each numbered D014 image and its caption as subject/composition context, not as an identity authority. Use D001 S004/S008 only for the approved matte rendering language. The approved Guruvayurappan sheet anchors Narayana identity in S003-S004. The older Bhattathiri sheet anchors the poet in S010.
